Use of Non-Conventional Energy
Sources for electrification
*381. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL
APTE:
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of NEW AND
RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have launched
certain schemes/programmes under the
non-conventional energy sources to
provide energy derived from wind, sun and
bio-gas to rural areas of the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the number of villages electrified
through solar and bio-gas energy during the
last two years, till date, State-wise; and
(d) the steps taken by Government to
promote NCES in the country, particularly
in remote rural villages?
Activities of Indian Council for
Philosophical Research
*382. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the activities of Delhi
and Lucknow centres of the Indian Council
for Philosophical Research and expenditure
incurred at both the centres;
(b) whether it is a fact that the Lucknow
centre does not have any campus and
valuable assets of the centre are lying
unused;
(c) whether it is also a fact that at present
ICPR is not being headed by an academi-
cian in the relevant discipline; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
Misuse of funds for Sarva Shiksha
Abhiyan by States
*383. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have come
across any misuse of funds by the States
which are implementing the Sarva Shiksha
Abhiyan;
(b) if so, the break-up of funds that
have been embezzled, State-wise during the
last three years;

121
(c) whether any penal action to
discipline and discourage the perpetrators
and also to freeze the fund disbursals to
the States have been initiated;
(d) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Hydro power potential in West Bengal
*384. SHRI TARINI KANTA ROY:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
refer to the answer to Unstarred Question
2195 given in the Rajya Sabha on the
19th March, 2007 and to  state:
(a) whether any survey of mini and
macro-hydro power potentiality in West
Bengal has ever been made apart from what
has been stated;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that no action has
yet been taken to tap hydro-power
potentiality in Rammam-I and Rammam-
III sources; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
Delayed private power generation
projects
*385. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the private
sector power generation projects are lagging
behind their schedules;
(b) if so, the details thereof, project-
wise; and
(c) the reasons therefor, project-wise?
Tribal literacy in Orissa
*386. SHRI BHAGIRATHI MAJHI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal to increase the tribal literacy rate
in Orissa where the literacy rate among the
tribals is the lowest in the country, being
about 37 per cent only against the national
average of 47 per cent;
(b) if so, the major steps Government
have initiated in this regard; and
(c) if not, whether Government would
include and initiate steps to increase the
literacy rate of tribes in the State?
Village electrification in
Assam
*387. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of POWER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been any major
initiatives for village electrification
programme in the country particularly in
Assam; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and what
steps are being taken by Government in
this regard?
Anganwadis sanctioned for Andhra
Pradesh
*388. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 8,000
Anganwadis have been sanctioned for
Andhra Pradesh under ICDS;
(b) the number of Anganwadi Centres
sanctioned and set up in Andhra Pradesh
under ICDS, year-wise; and
(c) how Government are implementing
the Supreme Court judgment that ICDS
should be extended not only to BPL families
but also to other eligible people?

Vision document 2015 on food
processing industries
2882. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have finalized
a vision document 2015 on food processing
industries to boost the growth of food
processing sector;
(b) if so, the salient features thereof;
and
(c) whether Government have identified
strategy to realize the vision and if so, the
details thereof?
Requirement of food processing
facilities
2883. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the requirement of food processing
facilities and the availability of such
facilities, State-wise;
(b) whether it is a fact that a huge
quantity of products suffer from want of
facilities leading to heavy loss to the
producers/farmers;
(c) the allocation made for cold storages/
warehousing facilities and how much has
been utilized during the last three years;
and
(d) whether there is a subsidy
component in this process and if so, the
details thereof?
Problems faced by food processing
sector
2884. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRA-
IAH: Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the challenges like antiquated laws,
fragmented processing capacities, poor
adoption of pre and post harvest
technologies, on-farm and off-farm losses
of fresh produce etc. that are being faced
by the food processing sector;
(b) whether Government propose to

668
reduce the high logistics costs which are
mainly due to the limitation of infrastructure
like roads, warehouses, carriers and cold
chains, etc.;
(c) if so, the details of policy initiatives
taken up so far particularly in Andhra
Pradesh; and
(d) the measures being initiated to meet
the challenges?
Opening of an elite college in Orissa
2885. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Orissa Government
proposes to open an elite college in mining,
mineral and metallurgy engineering;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of help both financial and
physical that is proposed to be provided
by the Centre to the State to set up this
institute?
Implications of SC verdict on
reservation
2886. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL:
SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry have analysed
the implications of the Supreme Court
verdict on OBC reservation in higher
educational institutions; and
(b) the steps proposed to be taken to
ensure the reservation to OBCs?
Kendriya Vidyalayas in Jharkhand
†2887. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the district-wise number of Kendriya
Vidyalayas in Jharkhand at present;
(b) whether any proposal regarding
opening of new Kendriya Vidyalaya in the
State is under consideration;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the action being taken in this regard?
Vacancies reserved for tribals
2888. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of vacancies of teachers
and professors which are reserved for tribals
in all the schools and colleges of the country
during the last five years; and
(b) the figures for the last three years of
appointment of tribals in Central schools,
Navodaya schools and other Government
institutions all over the country?
Central assistance for Mid-Day Meal
scheme
2889. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the Central assistance granted to
Karnataka under the Mid-Day Meal
scheme during the last three years ending
31st March, 2007, year-wise;
(b) the extent to which the funds under
the scheme were utilized by the State, year-
wise till 31st March, 2006, along with
State's share therein, year-wise; and

(c) whether the un-utilized funds under
the scheme are lapsed or allowed to be
carried forward to next year?

engineers in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether it is a fact that Government
have failed to utilize human resources and
infrastructure to hone the engineers in the
